correctness.rationale: Exact graph-definition proof: a mixed-layer connected dominating set requires a selected matching edge; any layer of size >=2 can replace an omitted same-layer vertex while retaining a matching edge; a singleton layer requires the opposite clique to be full. Count disjoint index-set pairs, then characterize inclusion-minimal sets. The independent adjacency/BFS/replacement checker verified the original definition and all formulas for all 87,360 subsets in H_3,...,H_8. This finite check is corroboration; Steps 1-5 prove all n>=3. Boundary n=3 merges the two minimal terms.

The conclusion remains subject to unindexed-priority risk; lack of search matches is not itself a uniqueness proof.
residual_risks: Unindexed, mislabeled or inaccessible prior work on the same single-exchange predicate may contain an equivalent exact count.

value.rationale: A natural family of connected n-regular graphs has a complete bivariate census of fault-tolerant connected monitoring sets. The minimum size stays 4 while inclusion-minimal sizes are exactly 4 and n+1; the latter occurs in precisely 2n patterns, creating an unbounded n-3 greedy/optimal gap. The structural split is not a routine parameter renaming or an arbitrary numerical slice and distinguishes optimization from irredundant solutions.
